problem: The population of pines in a forest increases by $100$ trees every year. What differential equation describes the rate of change of the population $P(t)$ of the pines? Assume that the time $t$ is measured in years.
worked_solution:
If the pines population is $P,$ then the rate of change of the population is $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in years.

Since $100$ new pines are added every year, the rate of change of the population of the pines is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=100.
$$
